# Summary

The chart is not being re-rendered when the height or width is changed using a variable

# Steps to reproduce

```python
height = st.slider('Chart height:', 0, 500, 400, 100)

df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=["lat", "lon"])

st.deck_gl_chart(
    viewport={
        'latitude': 37.76,
        'longitude': -122.4,
        'zoom': 11,
        'pitch': 50,
        'height': height,
    },
    layers=[{
        'type': 'HexagonLayer',
        'data': df,
        'radius': 200,

        'elevationRange': [0, 1000],
        'pickable': True,
        'extruded': True,
    }, {
        'type': 'ScatterplotLayer',

```

The graph should be re-rendered

There's no difference when we change the value

issue.title: Ability to update Deck.GL viewport dynamically

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
Steps to repro:

1) Run this file:

```python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(1000, 2) / [50, 50] + [37.76, -122.4],
    columns=['lat', 'lon'])

x = st.deck_gl_chart(
    viewport={
        'latitude': 0,
        'longitude': 0,
        'zoom': 11,
        'pitch': 50,
    },
    layers=[{
        'type': 'ScatterplotLayer',
        'data': df,
    }])

x.deck_gl_chart(
    viewport={
        'latitude': 37.76,  # ← this changed
        'longitude': -122.4,  # ← this changed
        'zoom': 11,
        'pitch': 50,
    },
    layers=[{
        'type': 'ScatterplotLayer',
        'data': df,
    }])
```

**Actual:** the chart is centered a (0,0), in the Atlantic ocean
**Expected:** the chart is centered at (37, -122)

**Complication:** need to figure out what the desired behavior is for when the user recenters the map via the UI, and then a script rerun is triggered.

My gut feeling is that if the rerun has the same `viewport` as from when before the user interacted (or, may if the proto being sent is the same), the user's interaction should take precedence. Otherwise, the new `viewport` setting should take precedence. This is similar to how we handle widgets.

issue.title: Propagate viewState changes to PyDeck

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
As described in #985 #1043, changes to initialViewState previously would not propagate to PyDeck after the initial load. This made it difficult to control PyDeck programmatically.

This PR resolves these issues by setting the viewState directly on the deck object. I also attempted to use `setState()` in order to avoid direct manipulation, but it didn't propagate properly. 

Additionally, I add `effects` in order to comply with the typings in https://github.com/danmarshall/deckgl-typings#readme, though I do not explicitly use them. Temporarily using these typings revealed a few others issues, which have been fixed below.

I'm a complete React/Typescript novice, so there may be some more idiomatic way to accomplish these changes; I'm open to suggestions!
